notes.b: The practical coursework is 20% of the total marks in Home Economics Scientific and Social. Each assignment is recorded in the SEC's digital Food Studies Practical Coursework Journal.
points: Each assignment is recorded under four headings: Investigation, Planning and Preparation, Implementation and Evaluation.
Investigation (analysis and research) is marked out of 32.
Planning and Preparation is marked out of 8, for the ingredients with quantities and costing and for the key equipment.
Implementation is marked out of 28, for the procedure followed, the key factors considered, and safety and hygiene.
Evaluation is marked out of 12, for the implementation and for the specific requirements of the assignment.
The four headings total 80 marks for each assignment.
For 2027 candidates present two of the five assignments the SEC set, and the two highest-scoring assignments count.

notes.b: Every assignment falls under one of five areas, and the investigation for that assignment covers the points set for its area.
points: Area A: Application of Nutritional Principles.
Area B: Food Preparation and Cooking Processes, involving new skills or equipment.
Area C: Food Technology.
Area D: Properties of a Food.
Area E: Comparative Analysis, including Sensory Analysis.
Area A: the nutritional needs being investigated, the appropriate meal-planning guidelines, and suitable or modified dishes.
Area B: the preparation process, skill or equipment, the key points for success, and dishes that illustrate it.
Area C: the processing method and its principles, containers, packaging and labelling, and suitable foods or dishes.
Area D: the definition of the property, the principles associated with it, and dishes that illustrate it.
Area E: the testing technique and its possible outcomes, the foods or products tested, and the conditions that must be controlled.

notes.h: Rules for dishes, sources and group work
points: Dishes must meet the requirements of the assignment.
A dish may not be repeated, or partially repeated, across assignments.
Fresh foods should be used rather than convenience foods.
Practical work may be done in pairs, or in groups for Area E only.
The written record must be the candidate's own work, even where practical work was shared.
Every area requires sources of information to be cited, and all sources must be referenced, including AI-generated material.

notes.h: The 2027 assignments: Areas A and B
notes.b: The SEC set five assignments for 2027. The theory for each is taught in the chapter named after it.
points: Assignment 1 (Area A): the challenges older people face in keeping a healthy diet; their nutritional needs and meal-planning guidelines; two-course main-meal menus; preparation of one main course. Theory: Meal Planning and Special Diets.

Assignment 2 (Area A): the causes and effects of iron deficiency; the nutritional needs and meal-planning factors for reducing the risk; two-course main-meal menus; preparation of one main course. Theory: Vitamins and Minerals, and Meal Planning and Special Diets.

Assignment 3 (Area B): commercially prepared filo and puff pastry, covering brands, forms, ingredients, cost, and sweet and savoury dishes; the key points for success with one of them; preparation of one dish; evaluation of the advantages and disadvantages of the chosen pastry. Theory: Cereals and Grains.

notes.h: The 2027 assignments: Areas D and E
points: No Area C assignment was set for 2027.

Assignment 4 (Area D): types of marinade and the dishes that use each; the benefits of marinating and its underlying principles; the key points for success; preparation of one marinated dish; evaluation of whether the marinade achieved its purpose. Theory: Meat: Selection, Properties, and Cooking, covering tenderising.

Assignment 5 (Area E): descriptive rating tests and their use in the food industry; the range of commercial granola, covering brands, ingredients, nutritional content and cost; a descriptive rating test on two similar brands using six agreed sensory attributes and star diagrams; comparison of the two sensory profiles. Theory: Food Additives and Processing, covering sensory analysis and evaluation.

keyTerms.definition: The analysis and research section of each coursework assignment, which cites all sources of information.
Testing food with the senses to describe its characteristics and to compare products.
A sensory test in which a panel rates agreed attributes of a product on a scale.
A radial chart in which each arm shows the rated strength of one sensory attribute, so that two products can be compared at a glance.
A seasoned liquid in which food is soaked before cooking to add flavour and tenderise it.
Very thin, stretched sheets of dough that are brushed with fat between layers and baked to a crisp finish.
A laminated pastry made from layers of dough and fat, rolled and folded so that it rises in the oven.
The comparison of two or more similar products by testing to identify their differences.
A prepared food that reduces preparation and cooking time, which coursework dishes should avoid in favour of fresh foods.

questions.prompt: Outline the four headings under which each Food Studies coursework assignment is marked, giving the marks for each.
questions.model: Investigation (analysis and research): 32 marks. Planning and Preparation (ingredients with quantities and costing, and key equipment): 8 marks. Implementation (the procedure followed, the key factors considered, and safety and hygiene): 28 marks. Evaluation (of the implementation and of the specific requirements of the assignment): 12 marks. Total for each assignment: 80 marks.

questions.prompt: Discuss what must be covered in an Area E coursework investigation, including the sensory test, the foods tested and the conditions that must be controlled.
questions.model: Area E is Comparative Analysis, including Sensory Analysis. The investigation must describe the testing technique and its possible outcomes. A descriptive rating test uses a panel that rates agreed sensory attributes, such as appearance, aroma, flavour, texture and aftertaste, for each product. The results can be shown on star diagrams so that the two sensory profiles can be compared. The foods or products tested, such as two similar brands of a product, must be identified with their ingredients, nutritional content and cost. The conditions to control include the place and timing of the test, the number and type of tasters, hygiene and equipment, the temperature at which the samples are served, the sample quantity and uniformity, the coding of samples and the order in which they are presented. Sources of information must be cited, and the written record must be the candidate's own work even where the practical work was done in a group.
